label: Syn3A
plain: A bacterium with a designed, minimised genome: 452 protein-coding genes kept from Mycoplasma mycoides, in a cell about 400 nm across with one membrane and no wall. It grows on its own in a rich medium, and its genome is smaller than that of any natural cell that does.

modelled.text: JCVI-syn3A is the project's minimal-cell track (decision D173, 14 November 2026), taken up from a note that proposes it as the first whole-cell validation organism for Cells: the decision adopted it as a track, run beside the current work. Nothing of it is in the engine yet: the project's record holds an evidence audit, capability probes of the engine as it stands, and a proposed first milestone, with no engine code written for it and nothing accepted. That milestone, on protein-free vesicles, tests membrane physics and not Syn3A.

record.where: D173: Syn3A becomes the minimal-cell track; no contact with authors

levels.label: One cell
levels.note: Drawn as a sphere 0.4 µm across with 500 ribosomes: round numbers for the smaller of the two cells that were measured. The larger one was about 0.5 µm across.

no_further_levels: A single-celled organism: each cell lives on its own, so there is no tissue, organ or body.

facts.label: Shape and size
facts.value: a sphere about 400 nm across; two cells measured in electron tomograms were 403 nm and 495 nm across

facts.label: Envelope
facts.value: one membrane; no cell wall and no periplasm

facts.label: Inside
facts.value: no nucleus: in electron tomograms the ribosomes are spread through the whole cell, with the chromosome among them

facts.label: Genes
facts.value: 493, of which 452 code for proteins; the genome record lists 455 protein products, 3 of them added for genetic manipulation

facts.label: Ribosome's size
facts.value: drawn as E. coli's ribosome, measured by the viewer from the coordinates of the Protein Data Bank's entry 7K00: as the ellipsoids of the same spread as their atoms, the large subunit 20.6 by 18 by 14.3 nm across and the small one 23.5 by 15.2 by 10 nm, their centres 10.4 nm apart, the whole 26.1 by 21.1 by 17.3 nm (its farthest atoms 26.8 by 24.3 by 20.6 nm). The entry 5MDZ gives 25.6 by 21.2 by 18.5 nm, within 1.2 nm of it. No structure of its own ribosome is among this file's sources. Gilbert and others 2021 took a ribosome to be about 20 nm across in their model of the cell, and found the ribosomes in their tomograms with a structure of E. coli's ribosome (the entry 5MDZ) as the template

facts.label: Ribosomes
facts.value: about 500 in a small cell: 503 or 684 counted in the cell 403 nm across, by two ways of counting, and 820 or 1,095 in the one 495 nm across

facts.label: Proteins
facts.value: about 77,000 molecules in an average cell, an estimate from proteomics (77,028 by the paper's table); 427 of the 452 kinds were detected, and the added marker tetM. An estimated 7,685 of the molecules are of the 99 kinds that this file's shelves place in or on the membrane

facts.label: Energy
facts.value: ATP from fermenting sugar; in the 2019 reconstruction of its metabolism, central metabolism is the only source of ATP

facts.label: Food
facts.value: glucose, amino acids, fatty acids and cholesterol, taken up from a rich medium that is not fully defined

facts.label: Division
facts.value: the division genes ftsZ and sepF are among 19 genes added to the smaller strain JCVI-syn3.0 to make this one, which gave it back a regular shape; a review reports that seven of the 19 are needed together for normal division

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: a genome designed and synthesised from that of Mycoplasma mycoides subspecies capri, strain GM12, and cut down to a minimum

ribosome.measured: The viewer's own measure from the entry's coordinates, by tools/measure_particle.py: each subunit as the ellipsoid of the same spread as its polymer atoms (model 1): along each of its own three axes a half-width of the square root of five times the atoms' variance; the farthest atoms beside it. The frame: origin at the centre of both subunits' atoms; y from the large subunit's centre to the small one's; x the whole particle's longest axis made square to y (the next one if the longest runs along y); z = x × y. The Protein Data Bank states no size.
ribosome.note: No structure of Syn3A's own ribosome is among its file's sources: it is drawn at E. coli's measure. Gilbert and others 2021 took a ribosome to be about 20 nm across in their model of the cell, and found the ribosomes in their tomograms with a structure of E. coli's ribosome (the entry 5MDZ) as the template.

proteins.membrane_from: the proteins that the species' own shelves place in or on the membrane

cap.membrane.note: Its one membrane holds the cell's ion and proton gradients. In the 2019 reconstruction of its metabolism the ATP synthase pushes protons out, against a passive leak of protons inwards; that is a model's reading, and no source read for this file measured the voltage of this strain.

cap.channels.why: No ion channel was found among its 455 proteins: none carries the signature of a channel family in Cells' catalogue, or of the bacterial channels for potassium, chloride, magnesium, water or membrane stretch, which the same search does find in other mollicutes. Its ions cross the membrane through transporters and pumps.

cap.pumps.note: Not the pumps of animal cells: it has no sodium-potassium pump. By its annotation, its ATP-driven ion movers are the ATP synthase, two P-type ATPases named as magnesium transporters, and a potassium uptake system.

cap.junctions.why: It lives as single cells and has no gap junctions: none of its proteins carries the signature of connexins or innexins.

cap.extracellular.note: Here it is the growth medium around the single cell, which the cell depends on. By the 2019 reconstruction of its metabolism it takes up glucose, amino acids, fatty acids and cholesterol from a rich medium.

cap.water.note: It has no cell wall: nothing but the membrane bounds its volume.

cap.calcium.why: It has no endoplasmic reticulum: it is a bacterium with a single membrane and no internal compartments, and none of its proteins carries the signature of the store's calcium pump or of its release channels.

cap.energy.note: Its ATP comes from fermenting sugar in the cytoplasm: in the 2019 reconstruction of its metabolism, central metabolism is the only source of ATP.

cap.mitochondria.why: It is a bacterium and has no mitochondria. Its ATP synthase sits in the cell membrane.

cap.circuits.note: At the chromosome, which lies in the cytoplasm: there is no nucleus. The 2019 paper notes how few regulatory proteins the minimised genome has left.

cap.grn.why: It forms no tissue, so there is nothing for gene networks to be coupled across. Gene expression within the one cell belongs with regulatory circuits.

cap.trafficking.why: It has no endoplasmic reticulum and no Golgi. By its annotation, new membrane proteins are put straight into the cell membrane by the Sec translocon and the YidC insertase.

cap.assembly.note: Its assemblies are its ribosomes, RNA polymerase and the ATP synthase. The designed protein cage that Cells models is not one of its proteins.

cap.machines.note: About 500 ribosomes, with RNA polymerase, the ATP synthase and the protein translocon. None of its proteins carries the proteasome's signature; its annotation lists the proteases FtsH and Lon.

left_out.says: the barrel drawn for its molecular machines
left_out.reason: the picture drew it as a proteasome's core, which this cell does not have, and in a cell this small that barrel stood among the largest things drawn
left_out.why: On 17 November 2026 the user asked for the molecular machines' barrel to be left out of the bacteria's picture for now, as the map's protein assembly was left out of every species on 15 November; it read as an assembly of molecules, and stood among the largest things drawn. Its place and its note stay in this file: take the flag out and the barrel is drawn again.

cap.secretion.note: By the 2019 reconstruction of its metabolism it releases the end products of sugar breakdown, lactate and acetate, into the medium and takes nutrients up. Signalling between its cells was not looked for.

cap.repair.note: The place would be its bare membrane. No source read for this file describes a membrane injury or its resealing in this organism.

cap.division.note: It grows and divides as a single cell. The division genes ftsZ and sepF are among 19 genes that were added to the smaller strain JCVI-syn3.0 to make it, which gave it back a regular shape; a review reports that seven of the 19 are needed together for normal division.

cap.replacement.why: It forms no tissue, so there is no neighbour for a new cell to replace.

cap.mechanics.why: It forms no sheet: its cells share no edges to pull on.

cap.sheet.why: It lives as single cells and forms no sheet of coupled cells.

breuer2019.text: Breuer and others (2019) Essential metabolism for a minimal cell. eLife 8:e36842.

gilbert2021.text: Gilbert and others (2021) Generating Chromosome Geometries in a Minimal Cell From Cryo-Electron Tomograms and Chromosome Conformation Capture Maps. Front Mol Biosci 8:644133.

zhang2023.text: Zhang and others (2023) Investigation of Genome Biology by Synthetic Genome Engineering. Bioengineering (Basel) 10(2):271. A review.

thornburg2022.text: Thornburg and others (2022) Fundamental behaviors emerge from simulations of a living minimal cell. Cell 185:345-360.e28. A whole-cell model of this organism: its own account of the cell's energy, its membrane proteins and its regulation is there.
